items.title: 66600_Teddy Wilson oral history interview
items.q: The interviewer mentions Thayer Jones in the context of bands playing his compositions, but Teddy Wilson does not respond with any personal anecdote, relationship, or specific knowledge about Thayer Jones himself.

ctx.x: Haydn the Paris symphonies, which was from the 1780's, and they did something from the 1880's. Now that's quite a span, quite a spectrum of musical styles -- and all of them were done with extraordinary excellence. The orchestra was great, the conductor was great and so forth.

I notice that in jazz, like for instance, you commented to Steven that Coltrane is his era -- you hear these bands like in North State Texas and so forth, all of them playing very well, doing the compositions of Thayer Jones, and all the people, with the Maynard Ferguson sound and the like -- but you never hear anybody play anything like Ben Moten or Fletcher Henderson, like Jay McShann, by anybody, or even the lesser known bands further back. And I find that you see, when the rock era came in, all this sort of…

And in the classical world, they've never said you're moving forward because the other is inferior. You add to it, but you keep it all together and the great masters of Europe that go all the way back to Michael Praetorius, even back to the Gregorian period, are still preserved to this day, but yet, very few people know of Benny Moten or Eddie Durham, and any of these people --
